form.hint: Hover a wheel line: it lights up orange and arrows with a label show what exactly changes. Drag along the arrows: bead seats and barrel floor — diameter, flanges — width, mounting face — offset, dashed spoke line — X-factor. Backspacing is calculated from width and offset. Presets are typical guides, not data for specific cars; they do not change the X-factor. Undo and redo: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z. The “Show tire” checkbox draws a tire around the wheel by size, e.g. 245/40; a tire narrower than the wheel is drawn stretched.

how.title: How to use the calculator
how.sub: Four steps to see in a minute whether a wheel will fit.
how.1.title: Set the dimensions
how.1.text: Pick a ready-made size from the list or enter diameter, width and ET offset. The switch at the top of the form changes millimeters to inches for diameter, width and backspacing; ET offset and X-factor are always in mm.
how.2.title: Drag the lines on the diagram
how.2.text: Hover a wheel line: it lights up, with arrows and a label. Drag the bead seats and barrel floor (diameter), the flanges (width), the mounting face (offset) or the dashed spoke line (X-factor).
how.3.title: Add a tire
how.3.text: Turn on “Show tire” and enter a size, for example 245/40. If the tire is narrower than the wheel it is drawn stretched, and an overly strong stretch triggers a warning.
how.4.title: Save or share
how.4.text: Press the Share button next to the form title: all parameters live in the link. Made a mistake? Use Undo and Redo (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z) or Reset.
terms.title: What the wheel parameters mean
terms.sub: A short note on every value the calculator changes.
terms.1.title: Diameter
terms.1.text: Bead seat diameter of the rim, usually in inches: 16, 17, 18. On the diagram it is the distance between the bead seats at the top and bottom.
terms.2.title: Width
terms.2.text: Distance between the rim flanges, usually in inches: 7, 8, 9.5. It decides which tires fit and how the wheel sits in the arch.
terms.3.title: ET offset
terms.3.text: Distance from the rim centerline to the mounting face, in mm. The higher the ET, the deeper the wheel sits in the arch; the lower, the further it sticks out.
terms.4.title: X-factor
terms.4.text: Distance between the mounting face and the inner surface of the spokes. It decides whether the brake caliper fits inside the wheel: too small an X-factor means the spokes hit the brakes.
terms.5.title: Backspacing
terms.5.text: Distance from the mounting face to the inner edge of the rim. Calculated automatically from width and offset.
terms.6.title: Stretch (“house” fit)
terms.6.text: The tire is narrower than the wheel: sidewalls slope inward from the rim flanges. It is seen in styling, but a strong stretch is unstable, so the calculator warns about it.
why.title: Why calculate in advance
why.sub: Wheels are bought once, and returning or redoing them can be costly and inconvenient.
why.1.title: Don’t buy blind
why.1.text: A few millimeters of offset or width change how the wheel sits relative to the arch and suspension. The diagram shows it before you buy.
why.2.title: Check the brakes
why.2.text: Look at the X-factor up front: a wheel with pretty spokes is useless if it does not clear the caliper.
why.3.title: Compare options
why.3.text: Ready-made sizes and undo let you quickly try several setups and go back to the best one.
why.4.title: Show your installer or friends
why.4.text: One link stores the whole configuration: send it in a chat and the other person sees the same dimensions and the same diagram.
why.note: The diagram is schematic: barrel, bead seat and spoke shapes are the same for every size, and presets are typical guides, not data for specific cars. Before buying, check the wheel, tire and vehicle manufacturer’s data and consult an installer.
faq.title: FAQ
faq.sub: Answers to what people most often ask when choosing wheels.
faq.1.a: It is the distance in millimeters from the rim centerline to the mounting face that presses against the hub. Positive ET moves the wheel deeper into the arch, negative ET pushes it outward.
faq.2.q: How does X-factor relate to brakes?
faq.2.a: X-factor shows how far the spokes sit from the mounting face. If it is too small, the spokes hit the brake caliper and the wheel cannot be turned or even bolted on fully.
faq.3.a: A small stretch is seen in practice, but the tire manufacturer defines the allowed rim width for a tire. A strong stretch is unstable: the bead can come off, pressure can be lost and handling suffers. The calculator flags such cases, but the final decision should follow the manufacturer’s data.
faq.4.q: Can I save the settings or send them to someone?
faq.4.a: Yes. The Share button next to the form title opens the share menu or copies a link to the current configuration. The parameters are stored in the address, so the link opens exactly the same diagram.
faq.5.a: Offset, backspacing and tire size calculations are exact for the values you enter, while the diagram itself is schematic and only for illustration. The real shape of a specific wheel and tire differs.
footer.text: Wheel fitment calculator: ET offset, width, diameter, X-factor, tire and stretch. The diagram is schematic, so check sizes against manufacturers’ data.
